newsitem.title: USA: South Jersey Gas granted rate increase.
newsitem.headline: South Jersey Gas granted rate increase.

text.p: South Jersey Gas Co said the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities has approved a $6 million annual increase in the company's base rates.
The board also approved a $2.5 million a year revenue reduction resulting from the South Jersey Industries Inc subsidiary's temperature adjustment clause, it said.
This mechanism protects utility sales from weather related swings by increasing or reducing rates when temperatures are at extremes above or below the 20-year average.

For the period ending May 31, 1996, South Jersey Gas said, temperatures in its service area were significantly lower than normal, resulting in the refund to be reflected with reduced rates from January 22 through May 31, 1997.

Spokeswoman Joanne M. Brigandi said the rate increase is the result of a settlement reached with the board's staff and intervenors, particularly South Jersey Gas industrial customers. The utility had requested a $26.5 million increase.
She said the settlement also allows a return on equity of 11.25 percent, down from the 11.5 percent allowed in the company's previous rate increase.
In 1996, Brigandi said, it earned a return of 14.3 percent. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
